LESSON: LISTENING AND SPEAKING 12.1.1 PRONUNCIATION AND VOCABULARY

Grade: Grade 6
Subject: ENGLISH LANGUAGE
Strand: Strand 12
Topic 12.1: Listening and Speaking 12.1.1 Pronunciation and Vocabulary
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 3

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Listening and Speaking 12.1.1 Pronunciation and Vocabulary, part of Strand 12 in Grade 6 ENGLISH LANGUAGE.

Key inquiry question: Why should you speak at the right speed, accurately, and with expression? 2. How do our faces, hands, and eyes help us communicate better?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

A. listen for specific details such as sounds words and expressions for effective oral communication,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Listening and Speaking 12.1.1 Pronunciation and Vocabulary in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

B. make oral presentations such as speeches accurately, with minimal hesitations and with expressions.

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Listening and Speaking 12.1.1 Pronunciation and Vocabulary in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

C. use non-verbal cues appropriately to enhance fluency,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Listening and Speaking 12.1.1 Pronunciation and Vocabulary in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

A. listen for specific details such as sounds words and expressions for effective oral communication,

   Listening and Speaking 12.1.1 Pronunciation and Vocabulary helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

B. make oral presentations such as speeches accurately, with minimal hesitations and with expressions.

   Listening and Speaking 12.1.1 Pronunciation and Vocabulary helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

C. use non-verbal cues appropriately to enhance fluency,

   Listening and Speaking 12.1.1 Pronunciation and Vocabulary helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

D. Suggested learning experiences (from KICD)

1. say words and phrases with the sounds / ʒ/ / ʤ/ correctly,

2. recite poems with words that have the sounds /ʒ/ / ʤ/,

3. Listen for specific details such as: fixed phrases: as long as, all the time, set on fire, from time to time, too bad, be in trouble; simile: as wide as the sky, as brave as a lion, as green as grass, as clear as crystal, as clear as 1.

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

1. say words and phrases with the sounds / ʒ/ / ʤ/ correctly,
2. recite poems with words that have the sounds /ʒ/ / ʤ/,
3. Listen for specific details such as: fixed phrases: as long as, all the time, set on fire, from time to time, too bad, be in trouble; simile: as wide as the sky, as brave as a lion, as green as grass, as clear as crystal, as clear as 1.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Listening and Speaking 12.1.1 Pronunciation and Vocabulary together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
• Communication: The learner’s ability to speak clearly and correctly is developed as they practise saying words

and phrases with the sounds / ʒ/ / ʤ/.

• Self-efficacy: The learner’s ability to confidently communicate is enhanced as they master the art of speaking

fluently while practising correct articulation of sounds.

103

Values:
Peace: This is enhanced as the learner avoids hurting others while speaking on environmental conservation or content

from other areas in class.

Unity: This is inculcated in the learner through collaboration with peers as they make presentations in class.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs):

Environmental Conservation: The learner is more informed on matters about the environment as they interact with

information on environmental conservation and speak on topics based on the same.

Link to other Learning Areas:

The learner is able to relate the concept of making oral presentations to their learning in Social Studies and other

learning areas.
